title: Flat extension preserves finite reflexive modules
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a flat homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] of commutative Noetherian integral domains [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $M$ be a finitely generated $A$-module. A module $N$ over a commutative ring $R$ is called reflexive when the evaluation map $N\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,R),R)$ is an isomorphism. If $M$ is reflexive over $A$, then $M\otimes_A B$ is a finitely generated reflexive $B$-module. No projectivity or local freeness of $M$, and no normality or finite-type assumption on either ring, is required.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-reflexive-saturated-free-embedding] over $A$ to the finite reflexive module $M$. Choose $r\ge0$ and an exact sequence $0\to M\xrightarrow{i}A^r\xrightarrow{q}N\to0$ with $N$ torsion free. This uses only that $A$ is a Noetherian domain and $M$ is finite and reflexive, all hypotheses of the item.

source.place: Tag 0EB9 (more-algebra-lemma-flat-pullback-reflexive), proof. First sentence, using Tag 0AV2.

proof.text: The flat-map definition [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] makes $B$ a flat $A$-module. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] to obtain an injective $i_B=i\otimes1$ and $\ker(q\otimes1)=\operatorname{im}i_B$. The last map $q_B=q\otimes1$ is surjective: express an element of $N\otimes_A B$ as a finite sum $\sum_j n_j\otimes b_j$, lift each $n_j$ to $x_j\in A^r$ using surjectivity of $q$, and use $\sum_j x_j\otimes b_j$. Hence $0\to M\otimes_A B\xrightarrow{i_B}A^r\otimes_A B\xrightarrow{q_B}N\otimes_A B\to0$ is short exact.

source.place: Tag 0EB9 (more-algebra-lemma-flat-pullback-reflexive), proof. Middle sentence, flat exactness; surjectivity spelled out on pure tensors.

proof.text: Choose generators $m_1,\ldots,m_s$ of $M$. Each $m\otimes b$, with $m=\sum_j a_jm_j$, equals $\sum_j f(a_j)b(m_j\otimes1)$, where $f:A\to B$ is the given homomorphism. Thus the finitely many $m_j\otimes1$ generate $M\otimes_A B$. The $B$-linear coordinate map $A^r\otimes_A B\to B^r$, $(a_i)\otimes b\mapsto(f(a_i)b)_i$, has inverse $(b_i)\mapsto\sum_i e_i\otimes b_i$. Their composites are identities by expansion in the coordinate basis and the tensor balancing relation. This proves that the middle module is finite free, also when $r=0$ or $s=0$.

source.place: Tag 0EB9 (more-algebra-lemma-flat-pullback-reflexive), proof. Finite generation and the finite-free tensor calculation written explicitly.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-flat-base-change-torsion-free] to $A\to B$ and the torsion-free module $N$ from Step 1. Its hypotheses are flatness and that both rings are domains; these are assumed. It follows that $N\otimes_A B$ is torsion free over $B$, for all nonzero scalars of $B$, not merely the scalars coming from $A$.

source.place: Tag 0EB9 (more-algebra-lemma-flat-pullback-reflexive), proof. Middle sentence, using Tag 0AXM.

proof.text: Transfer the short exact sequence of Step 2 through the coordinate isomorphism of Step 3. It embeds the finite $B$-module $M\otimes_A B$ in $B^r$ with torsion-free quotient $N\otimes_A B$ by Step 4. Since $B$ is a Noetherian domain, the converse implication of [lem-per-reflexive-saturated-free-embedding] proves that $M\otimes_A B$ is reflexive. Together with the finite generation proved in Step 3 this is every clause of the assertion; no normality, projectivity, local freeness, or finite-type hypothesis has been used.

source.place: Tag 0EB9 (more-algebra-lemma-flat-pullback-reflexive), proof. Last sentence, using Tag 0AV2 over the target ring.
